headline: Lima inflation reaches 5.25% in October, highest in over three years
summary: The annual inflation rate in Lima Metropolitan area climbed to 5.25% in October 2026, marking the highest level since August 2023.
why: Inflation data is a primary indicator for central bank policy. Rising price levels often force monetary authorities to maintain or increase interest rates to stabilize the currency and control purchasing power.

impacts.name: Peru
impacts.why: Higher inflation erodes consumer purchasing power and may lead to tighter monetary policy.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Persistent inflation typically prompts central banks to keep interest rates elevated, which can slow economic growth and impact local asset valuations.
